newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars firm after Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars firm after Fed meeting.

text.p: Japanese and U.S. interest rate futures on SIMEX both received a lift on Wednesday from the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave short-term interest rates unchanged at its policy-making meeting on Tuesday.

"The Euroyen and JGB (Japanese government bond) futures are going up on the Fed meeting. Now Japan is not under pressure to hike rates, especially with the yen already being so firm," a trader with a Japanese institution said.

Reports that Nikko Securities Investment Trust and Management Co, an affiliate of Nikko Securities Co Ltd, had conducted illegal bond trading and faced possible penalties from the Finance Ministry also underpinned Euroyen and JGB futures.
"The way the Euroyen has been traded by Japanese banks in the past few days indicates that they're not really expecting (Japan) to raise rates soon," a trader with a European futures house said.
He said December Euroyen faced good resistance at 99.00, but a breach of that level could push it up to 99.04 if any stop-loss buy orders were triggered.
The contract was up a tick against its IMM close of 98.97 at 0440 GMT after hitting a high of 98.99 on volume of 8,155 lots.
Dealers said activity was somewhat muted by a holiday in Singapore, though volumes were better than on an average holiday.
June JGBs were at 124.77 after climbing as high as 124.91, an area expected to pose some resistance, against their previous 124.45.
Eurodollar futures rose on the back of the Fed decision but dealers said further upside was likely to be limited as most participants believed a rate hike had merely been deferred.
"We saw some new buyers coming in in the morning. We might trade a couple of ticks higher but people are banking on a rate hike at the next meeting," the trader at the European house said.
September Eurodollars were at 93.985 at 0440 GMT against their IMM close at 93.955. December were at 93.770 against 93.735. Volume for both months was less than 5,000 lots.
